proof_summary: A binomial–Fibonacci identity gives \(2nS(n)=L_{2n}-1\), so integrality would force \(2n\mid L_{2n}-1\); congruences modulo \(4\) eliminate the cases \(3\mid n\) and even \(n\). For odd \(n\) with \(3\nmid n\), the identity \(L_{2n}-1=L_n^2+1\) rules out prime divisors \(p\equiv3\pmod4\), explicit recurrences modulo \(5,13,17\) handle the small exceptions, and a Fibonacci rank-of-apparition bound produces a smaller prime divisor of \(n\) from any remaining smallest prime, a contradiction.
